issues.description: getIamPolicy failure silently classifies image as not publicly shared, producing false PASS findings.
issues.detail: When getIamPolicy raises (e.g. permission denied, as test-image-3 simulates), the except branch logs and leaves publicly_shared=False. The check then reports PASS for an image whose policy was never read. A security check defaulting to PASS on error is the wrong failure mode; introduce an UNKNOWN/MANUAL tri-state so the postcondition is honest.

issues.description: Check name is inconsistent between PR description, CHANGELOG, and code identifiers.
issues.detail: PR description references compute_image_publicly_shared while the directory, CheckID, class, and CHANGELOG use compute_image_not_publicly_shared. The check name is the contract identifier callers and dashboards bind to. Pick one canonical name and propagate it everywhere before merge.

issues.description: Per-image getIamPolicy runs serially while sibling collectors use __threading_call__.
issues.detail: _get_images iterates project_ids and images serially, issuing one getIamPolicy call per image. Every other resource collector in compute_service.py uses the existing threaded helper. For projects with many images the wall-clock is N * RTT; match the existing pattern or document why not.

issues.description: Image model stores only a derived boolean, discarding the IAM bindings that justify it.
issues.detail: publicly_shared bakes one check's verdict into the data structure; the bindings (role, members) are dropped at construction time. Storing the raw public members or offending bindings on the Image ADT would let future checks and remediation reason about which role grants public access without re-fetching.

issues.description: Image listing does not filter for custom images despite spec claiming it does.
issues.detail: The PR text says the check evaluates custom images only, but images().list(project=project_id) applies no filter (family, deprecated.state, source). Either state the precondition in a one-line comment explaining why project-scoped list suffices, or apply an explicit filter so the code matches the spec.

issues.description: Tests pin the leaky failure behavior rather than asserting the intended contract.
issues.detail: test-image-3 triggers an exception in getIamPolicy and tests assert publicly_shared=False, conflating 'truly not shared' with 'policy unreadable'. No test exercises what the check reports when IAM is unreadable end-to-end. The most security-relevant failure path is the one not proved; fixing the postcondition will be a test-breaking change.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the check is small and follows surrounding GCP idioms, but has one consequential defect: getIamPolicy failures silently degrade to publicly_shared=False, producing PASS findings for images whose policy was never read — the wrong failure direction for a security tool. A naming inconsistency between the PR description (compute_image_publicly_shared) and the shipped artifacts (compute_image_not_publicly_shared) must be reconciled. Secondary concerns: the image collection is serial while every other collector in the file is threaded, the Image ADT discards the bindings that justify its boolean verdict, the 'custom images' precondition is unenforced, and tests pin the leaky behavior rather than the intended contract. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK, primarily on the unknown-policy postcondition and the name.
